title: roster
description: runtime -> every agent: the fleet roster, the runtime's most recent word about which instances it has admitted, written once for the whole fleet to a location the deployment designates and exposes read-only to each agent it points at the roster. amap-spec v3.1.0 DRAFT (the draft's section "The Fleet Roster"). EXISTENCE IS NOT AUTHORISATION: a member's presence says the instance exists, never that this agent may address it or that a submission to it will be accepted; authorisation is evaluated by the runtime at submit time and only the result reports what happened. NOT A SOURCE OF THE READER'S IDENTITY: the reader's own address may appear, and attribution stays the namespace a file arrived in. A runtime MUST NOT read this file back. The file MAY be absent; absent or stale means unknown, never an empty fleet. Runtime-authored: envelope is OPEN at every level — a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognize; emitting an unrecognized member remains producer non-conformance.

router.description: the publishing runtime's own address, one bare addr-spec. Never appears in members.

written_at.description: RFC 3339, the publishing runtime's clock. The only staleness signal a consumer gets; an honest marker, not a freshness guarantee.

interval_s.description: OPTIONAL: the runtime's nominal rewrite interval in seconds, so a consumer can judge written_at against it. Omitted when the runtime does not know it.

members.description: the instances the runtime has admitted, sorted by address. Always present; never written as empty when membership is unknown (the previous file is left to age instead). The router is never a member.

address.description: the member's address, one bare addr-spec.

state.description: OPEN advisory vocabulary; "admitted" is the only value defined at this version. A consumer MUST tolerate an unknown value as opaque.
